label: M-03
title: PhusdStableMinter's daily phUSD issuance cap governs only half the phUSD an annihilation issues: a cap of X permits 2X
fingerprintNote: sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass)[:16] - legacy form, empty entryPoint. Carried verbatim from sanitized.json; reproduces from fingerprintBasis.

classification.assetImpact: No direct asset loss. The impact is on the protocol's ONLY per-day issuance control: a maxMintPerDay of X permits 2X of phUSD to be issued, and the mis-sizing is invisible because the counter reports 100% utilisation at 50% of real issuance. Antimatter has no cap of its own, no pause, and mint() (:179) has no supply ceiling, so this rail is the sole quantitative bound on the uncollateralised issuance of DEDUP-004/M-02.
attackPath: 1. Operator sets maxMintPerDay = X for a stablecoin, intending X phUSD/day of issuance.
2. Antimatter routes only the stable leg through PhusdStableMinter.mint (:227), which charges the counter amount*rate/1e18.
3. The antimatter leg is minted by Antimatter itself at :236 on its own FlaxToken authorisation, where the counter cannot see it. Issuance is amount*(1 + rate/1e18).
4. In ONE transaction the intended cap is exceeded outright - deterministic replay: cap 10,000e18, a single annihilateFrom of 6,000e18 charges 6,000e18 but delivers 12,000e18.
classification.likelihood: Certain - it is not conditional on anything; every annihilation under-charges by exactly the same factor.
classification.assumptions: exchangeRate == 1e18 gives the flat 2x; the true divisor is (1 + exchangeRate/1e18) and moves with the rate (see M-04).
classification.externalRequirements: maxMintPerDay set non-zero, i.e. the operator is relying on the rail at all.

justification: ADJUDICATING THE CONFLICT the sanitizer flagged (CODE-003 conceded 'a downgrade to Low is defensible'). HELD AT MEDIUM. The Low argument is honest - no asset loss and no attacker-specific gain - but it mis-frames the impact class: C4 Medium covers 'the function of the protocol ... could be impacted', and the function impaired here IS a safety control. The protocol's only issuance rail is off by 2x in the unsafe direction, silently, on a token half of whose issuance is structurally uncollateralised; and the operator has no way to notice, because the counter reads fully utilised exactly when it has permitted double. A control that lies about its own utilisation is worse than an absent control, because it manufactures false confidence at the moment it matters most. FOOTGUN TEST (Law 3): a competent, non-malicious operator entering X as a daily phUSD issuance cap WOULD be surprised that 2X is issued; discovering it requires knowing a second contract holds an independent FlaxToken mint authorisation. Surprise => footgun => in scope, at honest severity. Not High: no theft, no specific victim, no attacker gain beyond what the design already grants. Evidence: two invariants broken on two independent engines, a Medusa counterexample measuring exactly 2.000x in a single call, a deterministic non-fuzz replay, and an anti-vacuity check confirming the minter's cap was LIVE in the harness (121 swallowed inner reverts dominated by 'Daily mint limit exceeded') - so the failure is not an artefact of an inert control. Deliberately NOT collapsed with M-01/DEDUP-003 (unvalidated decimals) or M-05/DEDUP-006 (shared-budget DoS): same neighbourhood, different root causes and different mitigations.
recommendation: Route the antimatter leg through PhusdStableMinter so one counter sees the whole issuance, or add an equivalent per-period cap on Antimatter's own leg at :236, or (weakest) rename/document maxMintPerDay as a per-stable DEPOSIT throttle so operators size it correctly.

additionalContext.strongestFraming: BOTH RETAINED BY DESIGN - CODE-003's code framing (which line bypasses which counter, and that the antimatter leg is the structurally uncollateralised half) AND ECON-002's operator/economic framing (the breaker under-counts by exactly 2x at the moment it is most needed). Neither subsumes the other; the task's instruction to keep both is honoured verbatim below.
additionalContext.rootCause: Antimatter routes the stable leg through PhusdStableMinter.mint (which charges maxMintPerDay with phUSDAmount) but mints the antimatter leg itself on its own FlaxToken authorisation, where the counter cannot see it. Issuance is amount*(1 + rate/1e18); cap consumption is amount*rate/1e18.
additionalContext.impact: The only per-day issuance rail anywhere on the annihilation path is exactly half the size its operator configured, and the mis-sizing is invisible: the counter reports 100% utilisation, not 50%. Antimatter has no cap of its own, no pause, and mint() (:179) has no supply ceiling.
additionalContext.footgunTest: Law 3 - a competent, non-malicious operator entering X as a daily phUSD issuance cap WOULD be surprised that 2X is issued. The consequence requires knowing a second contract holds an independent FlaxToken mint authorisation. Surprise => footgun => in scope.
additionalContext.safeConfigGuidance: PRESERVED FROM ECON-002 VERBATIM: 'Until the code is changed, set maxMintPerDay to HALF the phUSD issuance you intend to permit, for every stablecoin that Antimatter can annihilate - and only while exchangeRate == 1e18. The correct divisor is (1 + exchangeRate/1e18), so it changes the moment the rate is moved (see DEDUP-005). Do not treat maxMintPerDay as a phUSD-issuance cap; it is a per-stable deposit throttle that happens to be denominated in phUSD.'
